TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Kai Islands and the Biak enclave
DATE 21 November 2028 · 0350 local
SIDE Royal Australian Navy
WINDOW 70 min, closes at 105
Tu-214R reconnaissance. Photo: Japan Ministry of Defense / JASDF · CC BY 4.0 · cropped
"Air superiority is not guaranteed. It must be earned every day."
- Gen. Kenneth S. Wilsbach, Chief of Staff, US Air Force, 2025

KAI ISLANDS, 0350. Last night's imagery shows the enclave's new pads on Biak: two Fattah-1 launchers, a Fattah-2, an Emad and a Shahed 238 battery with eight jet drones. Everything on them reaches Langgur. A Tu-214R has flown the same track south towards the Kai group three nights running; tonight it will be looking for the batteries.

On Kai Kecil: a THAAD launcher with its AN/TPY-2, a Patriot PAC-3 launcher with its radar, and a US Army Steelfin battery, the first of its kind deployed outside a range. EAGLE II 31 and 32 are up out of Langgur with ARRW and SENTRY 05, an RAAF Triton, is off Biak to find the pads for them.

Destroy three of the five launchers and keep the strip in action. If Second Ring took down the S-350 and S-300 radars on the fourteenth, the pads have no cover; if it did not, the S-350 is still over them. Tual's ferry and its fishing boats are out tonight.
Wing Commander Daniel Ward, Air Component, RAAF Tindal; Captain Ratna Prasetyo, Indonesian Navy (TNI-AL), for the strip
COMMANDER'S INTENT

Five launchers on the Biak pads: two Fattah-1, a Fattah-2, an Emad and a Shahed 238 battery, and Langgur is three hundred and forty miles away, which is in range of all of them. The batteries hold the strip; the F-15EXs go for the launchers as soon as the Triton finds them. Each ballistic launcher has one round. The longer they stand, the more of them get to use it. Prasetyo's people are on that strip; so are the fuel bladders The Open Door flew on.
• Destroy three of the five launchers on Biak
• Keep the Langgur strip in action
• Lose nothing of the THAAD battery
• Shoot down the Tu-214R
• Harm no ferry or fishing boat

THAAD with AN/TPY-2, Patriot PAC-3 with AN/MPQ-65, a Steelfin battery, the Langgur strip; two F-15EX with ARRW and an RAAF Triton. Opposing: two Fattah-1, a Fattah-2 and an Emad launcher, a Shahed 238 battery, a Tu-214R, and the S-350 if Second Ring did not take it down. Neutral: the Tual ferry and fishing boats.

The planned window is 70 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 35 minutes more; the operation is closed at 105 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
